      "text": "This happens frequently on Linux (KDE Plasma) with Discord. In many cases, Discord\u0027s WebRTC layer on Linux only lists **\"System Default\"** instead of individual hardware names, or it is running in a sandbox (like Flatpak) that restricts device enumeration.\n\n---\n\n### 1. Discord routes through your system\u0027s \"Default\" device\nSince Discord is set to **System Default**, it will automatically use the device selected with the blue radio dot in your KDE audio settings (which is already set to **HyperX Cloud III Pro** in your screenshots).\n\nTo make sure audio is actively routing properly:\n1. In Discord, click **Mic Test** (or join a voice channel).\n2. Open your system\u0027s **Audio Volume** window (the window in your 2nd/3rd screenshots).\n3. Click the **Applications** tab at the top.\n4. Locate **Discord** while the mic test is active, and ensure its input and output streams are assigned to your **HyperX Cloud III Pro**.\n\n---\n\n### 2. If you are using Discord via Flatpak (Most Common Issue)\nIf Discord was installed through Flatpak/Discover, sandbox permissions might be blocking direct audio device enumeration:\n\n* **Fix via Terminal:** Run the following command to ensure Discord has full PulseAudio/PipeWire socket access:\n  ```bash\n  flatpak override --user --socket\u003dpulseaudio com.discordapp.Discord\n  ```\n* **Fix via GUI:** Open **Flatseal** (if installed), select **Discord**, scroll down to **Sockets**, and make sure **PulseAudio / Sound** is enabled.\n* Restart Discord afterward.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Reset Discord Voice Settings\n1. In Discord, go to **User Settings** $\\rightarrow$ **Voice \u0026 Video**.\n2. Scroll all the way to the bottom and click **Reset Voice Settings**.\n3. Turn off **\"Automatically Determine Input Sensitivity\"** to see if the yellow/green input bar picks up your microphone levels during testing.\n4. If available under *Advanced*, try changing the **Audio Subsystem** between **Standard** and **Legacy**.\n\n---\n\n### 4. Alternative for Linux (Vesktop / WebCord)\nThe official Discord Linux client uses an outdated Electron framework that has long-standing audio device and screensharing bugs on Linux. If you want proper PipeWire device detection, screensharing with audio, and lower resource usage, consider using **Vesktop** (available directly in the KDE Discover Software Center).",
